mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points over one month signals labor market tightening, which may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.3pp in a month, but the S&P 500 still shows positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A strong housing market, as indicated by increasing housing starts (HOUST), signals robust consumer demand, which may drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase by more than 5% in a month, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) show simultaneous increases, it indicates a strong labor market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase simultaneously, but the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strong supply chain and economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth is strong but inflation (CPIAUCSL) is also high, it may lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns as inflationary pressures could erode corporate margins.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth is strong and CPIAUCSL is high, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) may signal the end of the economic cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp in 2 months during a late-cycle expansion, but the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) may indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If real consumer spending increases by more than 2% in a month, but the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns, the hypothesis is falsified.
